qc.label_under_test: The future auxiliary 'will' (and 'll), strongest in relative clauses and questions ('which will', 'How will'); quiet on the noun 'will', past-tense rewrites and other modals.

neighbours.label: English future/prospective auxiliary: 'will', 'll, won't and hypothetical 'would', where a bare verb comes next; strongest in relative clauses and questions ('which will', 'Who will', 'Will you'); weak on could/should/must, quiet on noun 'will', a name Will mid-sentence, past/present tense and most non-English futures.
fire: The bridge, which will open next spring, links the two villages.
Who will take care of the garden while we're away?
Will you help me carry these boxes upstairs?
I'll call you as soon as the train arrives.
She won't believe what happened at the meeting.
If I had more time, I would learn to play the cello.
The committee will decide the matter on Friday.
They'll probably finish the roof before the rain starts.
quiet: The disaster took decades to reverse.
The bridge, which opened last spring, links the two villages.
Who took care of the garden while we were away?
Did you help me carry these boxes upstairs?
I called you as soon as the train arrived.
She doesn't believe what happened at the meeting.
Since I have more time, I am learning to play the cello.
